analysis.title: US Networking: Connecting the dots... A primer on networking equipment in the age of AI
key_insights: Bernstein initiated coverage of US Networking and Communications Equipment on 9/29 with a positive view. This note is a primer for investors new to the space, with details in the initiation 'US Networking: Scaling the bandwidth wall'.
Networking devices connect other devices and solve four problems: forwarding, performance, reliability and security. Networking is an $89B sector within a $5.6T annual IT spend market (Gartner).

Product categories are switching, enterprise networking, optical transport and transceivers. Coverage also includes components, notably optical fiber and optical modules. Customers are enterprises, service providers and hyperscalers.
2025 market sizes: optical fiber $41.9B, transceiver $38.9B, enterprise WAN $28.5B, back-end switching $20.1B, front-end switching $18.5B, enterprise LAN $16.6B, optical transport $14.4B.

Networking stocks have historically been among the worst performing tech subsectors. Bernstein attributes this to service provider exposure (saturated, replacement-driven spend) and to cloud, where hyperscalers insource software and services and bypass OEMs such as Cisco, Arista and HPE Juniper in favor of EMS/ODM vendors like Hon Hai and Accton.
Arista is the exception on cloud. Its EOS software is differentiated even for hyperscalers, so it has taken share at Meta and Microsoft.
Networking has re-rated on AI because accelerator compute performance has outscaled network performance, creating a 'bandwidth wall' in which networking is the bottleneck to AI performance.

New AI network architectures: scale-up (within a rack), scale-out (across racks), scale-across (between data centers) and scale-in (end users to accelerated compute, an Nvidia branding of the front-end network).

Bernstein sizes scale-across retrofits at about $8.9B global TAM from 117 new data center links at roughly $243M revenue per link. A Stargate-based sizing gives about $8B, or 2.2% of total AI training spend.
Ciena's CFO Marc Graff expects scale-across to be 'about an $8 to $10 billion dollar market' by 2029.
Bernstein sees scale-across as a model-training story, arguing latency matters less for inference and agentic workloads than commonly assumed.
Bernstein forecasts 18.1% 2026-28 networking market CAGR, with cloud/data center at 38.8%, enterprise at 9.4% and service provider at 4.3%. The market goes from $120B in 2026E to $186B in 2028E.

AI accelerator chiplet-adjusted shipments are expected to double 2025-28E (14,696K in 2025 to 36,037K in 2028E). AI back-end switching revenue is projected to rise from $20.1B in 2025 to $50.1B in 2027E and $116.4B in 2030E (Dell'Oro).
Cisco's hyperscaler orders reached $5.3B by CYQ2 2026, ahead of its full-year guide of $5B by CYQ4 2026. Nokia raised its Optical and IP Networks growth guide to 18-20% from 10-12%.

Ultra Ethernet, an open standard backed by Arista, HPE, Cisco, Microsoft, Oracle and Meta, is the multi-vendor alternative to Nvidia's proprietary InfiniBand. Standard Ethernet struggles with packet loss in spiky AI scale-out traffic.
Co-packaged optics (CPO) have been delayed and cost about 10% more than pluggables (Asia tech hardware team estimate). Near-packaged optics (NPO) are filling the gap and are easier to manufacture.
Networking is the most expensive component group per server rack in the cost breakdown. Networking sub-total per rack rises from $134K (H100 DGX x8) to $628K (GB200 NVL72) and $1,267K (VR NVL72).
Bernstein ratings: Outperform on ANET ($250), CLS ($520), CIEN ($440), LITE ($1,220), COHR ($350). Market-Perform on CSCO ($110), GLW ($140), HPE ($62).
Bernstein argues that not all networking technology moves stocks. Exhibit 3 shows WiFi cycle release dates have little connection to CSCO, ANET and JNPR stock moves.

market_movers.rationale: Quality compounder with further upside to numbers from share gain.
The OpenAI Jalapeno program's impact is not fully priced into 2027-28 numbers. The 10/27 analyst day could be a significant catalyst.
Likely supply constrained near term, but improving supply should unlock revenue upside. Longer-term growth expectations and valuation are undemanding.
Optical growth story should continue, and Lumentum benefits from high incremental margins.
Benefits from increasing optical adoption, with a call option on a potential VCSEL revival.
Pivot from hardware to software and deceleration in the software business limit enthusiasm.
Bernstein struggles to get comfortable with management's growth frameworks, even with significant upside from accelerator content.

Networking wins with Oracle and Vultr and higher networking guidance are encouraging, but sustained improvement depends on fixing execution issues and below-market growth. Recent growth is driven more by the traditional server business.

sector_views.rationale: AI-driven hyperscaler demand and the bandwidth wall make networking a structural AI beneficiary. Bernstein forecasts 18% market CAGR for 2026-28, with 39% from cloud/data center.

earnings_insights: Celestica has an analyst day on 10/27, which Bernstein sees as a potential catalyst.
risk_factors: CPO rollout delays create uncertainty on timing for hyperscaler optical solutions.
Cloud adoption has been a headwind for most networking OEMs because hyperscalers insource software and work directly with EMS/ODM vendors.
Service provider exposure has historically slowed growth because that market is saturated.
Ciena is supply constrained in the near term.
HPE has a history of execution issues and below-market growth.
It remains unclear how differentiated Nvidia's scale-in is from existing front-end solutions.
The number of scale-across links that actually get built is not yet known.

Exhibit 1 shows the 2025 IT spend split: IT Services 31%, Communications Services 23%, Software 23%, Devices 14%, Servers 7%, Enterprise Network Equipment 2%, Storage 1%.
Exhibit 8 shows AI accelerator chiplet-adjusted shipments of 3,494K in 2023, 8,397K in 2024, 14,696K in 2025, 20,150K in 2026E, 25,822K in 2027E and 36,037K in 2028E.
Exhibit 9 shows AI back-end switching revenue of $8,087M in 2024, $20,056M in 2025, $30,612M in 2026E, $50,139M in 2027E, $72,428M in 2028E, $94,404M in 2029E and $116,403M in 2030E.

tension_points.bull_case: Bandwidth wall makes networking a structural AI winner. Bernstein forecasts 38.8% cloud/data center CAGR for 2026-28 and sees scale-across as an $8-10B opportunity.
tension_points.bear_case: Networking has historically underperformed due to service provider exposure and hyperscaler insourcing. CPO delays and uncertainty over how many scale-across links get built add risk.

theme_stances.key_argument: Compute performance has outscaled network performance, so networking is the bottleneck and its stocks are structural AI winners.
theme_stances.evidence: the bandwidth wall explains why networking stocks have become structural AI winners

theme_stances.key_argument: Retrofitting existing data centers and building new links is a roughly $8-9B opportunity, driven by model training needs.
theme_stances.evidence: We believe there is huge potential for upside in scale across.
